name: Mauve brown
lede: Mauve brown is the English name our data gives to Hatobanezumi, a traditional Japanese color whose name translates as "dove feather grey."

sections.title: A translated Japanese grey
sections.body:
Our data files this as the English name for *Hatobanezumi* (鳩羽鼠), a traditional Japanese color name meaning "dove feather grey" [1]. It is also recorded in English sources as Reddish umber, a near-exact duplicate by our computed color distance (0.0 units) [2]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 42, chroma 11, hue 27 degrees: a dark, muted red-brown, far duller than any true mauve [1].

Our naming data files it as a family-word variant of [[mauve]], though the two colors share only the word, not the hue [1]. A Japanese fashion-history reference in our data groups it with *Rikyū-nezumi*, one of the roughly forty-eight browns and hundred greys named in Edo-period Japan, about 9.8 units away by measured distance [3]. We have not traced who coined the English name Mauve brown, or when; that is undocumented here [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 232, as photographed (112 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it more common than 61 percent of the named colors we track [4]. [[painter:claude-monet|Claude Monet]] used it most: it appears in 5 of his 50 works here, 6.8 times the rate of the museums those works come from, 5.7 times as photographed [4]. It is most over-represented in paintings from France, at 2.0 times the expected rate (38 of 3,443 paintings), and peaks in the 1900s at 2.5 times the expected rate [4].
